questions.q: What does gang scheduling guarantee that Kubernetes' default scheduler does not?
options: That Pods are always scheduled onto the cheapest available nodes
That a job's Pods are only placed once there is enough capacity for all of them at once — all or nothing, never a partial start
That Pods are scheduled in alphabetical order by name
That every Pod gets exactly one GPU regardless of its resource request
questions.explain: Gang scheduling's defining guarantee is all-or-nothing placement: a job's full set of Pods is scheduled together, or none of them are scheduled at all.

questions.q: Why is a 'partial start' (e.g. 50 of 64 Pods running) actively harmful for a distributed training job, rather than just slow?
options: It isn't harmful — training jobs run fine with any subset of ranks present
The Master's init_process_group blocks waiting for every rank to join, so the 50 running Pods hold GPUs idle while doing no useful work, and two such jobs can even deadlock each other
Partial starts cause immediate data corruption in the model weights
Kubernetes automatically kills any Pod that starts before its peers
questions.explain: torchrun's rendezvous on the Master blocks until every rank connects. A partial start means the Pods that did schedule hold GPUs that sit idle, and competing partially-scheduled jobs can deadlock, each holding resources the other needs.

questions.q: In a Volcano PodGroup spec, what does minMember control?
options: The minimum CPU request per Pod
The minimum number of Pods that must be schedulable together before Volcano will place any of them
The minimum number of nodes in the entire cluster
The minimum GPU driver version required
questions.explain: minMember sets the threshold for gang scheduling: Volcano holds the job's Pods Pending until at least that many (here, all 64) can be scheduled simultaneously.

questions.q: Why specifically can't a distributed training job just 'run with the ranks it has' the way a Deployment can run with fewer replicas?
options: Because torchrun doesn't support fewer than the full specified world size at all, under any circumstance
Because NCCL's collective operations (like AllReduce) are synchronous across every participating rank — there is no partial-rank version of a collective call
Because Kubernetes forbids jobs with fewer than their requested replica count from running
Because GPUs physically cannot communicate unless all 512 are present
questions.explain: Collective communication primitives block until every rank in the group reaches the call. There's no mechanism to proceed with a subset — which is exactly why a half-scheduled training job just hangs instead of running degraded.

questions.q: In the PodGroup example, why is minResources set to the full 512 GPUs rather than a smaller number?
options: It's an arbitrary default value with no real effect
It ensures Volcano won't begin placing any of the job's Pods unless the cluster can satisfy the entire 512-GPU request in one pass, matching minMember: 64
512 is the maximum GPU count Volcano supports per PodGroup
It reserves 512 GPUs permanently even when the job isn't running
questions.explain: minResources paired with minMember expresses the full gang-scheduling requirement: the scheduler only proceeds once it can satisfy the complete resource footprint for the complete set of Pods at once.
